newsitem.title: INDIA: WEEK AHEAD-India's volatile stocks to lose momentum.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD-India's volatile stocks to lose momentum.

text.p: India's overheated stock markets are likely to cool this week with market players unwinding positions after a steep rise in interest costs, dealers and analysts said at the weekend.
Carry-forward rates leapt to an annualised 40-45 percent on Saturday at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) against 15-17 percent a week ago.

Antony Sequeira, managing director of Arcadia Share & Stock Brokers, said the higher charges -- for carrying forward transactions from one weekly settlement to another -- reflected huge overbought positions.
But he said the markets were likely to remain volatile and unpredictable, with continued focus on speculative plays.
"It'll be in a trading range with bouts of optimism and pessimism driving prices with probably high volatility."

The BSE's benchmark 30-share index closed last week with a minor gain of 4.03 points at 3,422.35 after a roller-coaster ride that saw the index hitting a five-month high of 3,812.31 during an early rally on Thursday.
By the close on that day, the index had tumbled to end at a provisional 3,453.61 points. On Friday, the index eased a further 33.53 points.
After rising more than 12 percent in seven straight days, the index had lost over 10 percent from its peak in two days in record trader-driven volumes, analysts said.

Market-regulator the Securities & Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said on Friday after a meeting with the heads of major bourses it was satisfied with measures taken by the stock markets chiefs to monitor trading.
SEBI had convened the meeting to find ways to rein in excessive speculation and wide price swings.

"While there has been some institutional activity, it has been only in selective stocks. We continue to believe that the market is in a trading range," said Sanjeev Mohta, research head at James Capel B&K.
He recommended investors buy quality stocks that had underperformed in the recent rally. "This is probably one of the best times to reshuffle one's portfolio," he said in a note.
Mohta's top buys comprised Indian Hotels, and auto stocks Tata Engineering & Locomotive Company and Mahindra & Mahindra.
Other foreign funds also saw a silver lining in the longer term.
Lehman Brothers said in a report it was overweighting the Indian stockmarket and set a target of 3,900 for the BSE index over 12 months.

"Given our forecast for a strong economic recovery and continued forecast declines in interest rates, we recommend moving away from stables (stocks) and selectively towards cyclicals," said its senior strategist Abhijit Chakrabortti.
